title: Product of Segments of Chords OQ-01: 3D and General Generalization
description: Formal proof that the intersecting chords theorem (power of a point) extends to spheres in ℝ³ and to any real inner product space: the product of chord segment lengths through an interior point equals r² − d², invariant across all secant lines.

meta.author: Lean Genius
originalContributions: Dimension-independent proof of the chord quadratic equation in any real inner product space
Power of a point theorem for spheres in arbitrary inner product spaces (not just 2D)
Explicit 3D corollary with Sphere3D structure and EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)
Vieta product formula applied to derive |t₁|·|t₂| = r² − ‖P−O‖²

overview.historicalContext: The power of a point theorem has roots in ancient Greek geometry: Euclid's Elements Book III, Propositions 35–37 state equivalent results about chords and secants in circles. The modern algebraic statement — that for two chords intersecting at P inside a circle, $PA \cdot PB = PC \cdot PD$ — was systematized by Jakob Steiner (1796–1863), who introduced the term 'power of a point' (*Potenz eines Punktes*) in 1826. Steiner defined the power as $d^2 - r^2$ for exterior points and $r^2 - d^2$ for interior points, valid for all secants. The theorem appears as Wiedijk theorem #55 for the 2D circle case. The natural open question — does it generalize to spheres in $\mathbb{R}^3$ or higher dimensions? — is answered affirmatively here. The key insight is that the proof requires only inner product structure: the expansion $\|P + t\,\text{dir}\|^2 = \|P\|^2 + 2t\langle P, \text{dir}\rangle + t^2$ and Vieta's formula work identically in any real inner product space, making the theorem dimension-free.
overview.problemStatement: Prove that for a sphere with center $O$ and radius $r$ in any real inner product space, if $P$ is an interior point ($\|P-O\| < r$), then for any unit direction $\text{dir}$, the two intersection parameters $t_1, t_2$ of the line $P + t \cdot \text{dir}$ with the sphere satisfy $|t_1| \cdot |t_2| = r^2 - \|P-O\|^2$. In particular, this product is independent of $\text{dir}$.
overview.proofStrategy: The chord intersection equation $\|P - O + t \cdot \text{dir}\| = r$ expands via the inner product to $t^2 + 2t\langle Q, \text{dir}\rangle + (\|Q\|^2 - r^2) = 0$ where $Q = P - O$. This is a monic quadratic in $t$ with Vieta product $t_1 \cdot t_2 = \|Q\|^2 - r^2$. Since $P$ is interior, $\|Q\| < r$, so $t_1 \cdot t_2 < 0$ (opposite signs). Therefore $|t_1| \cdot |t_2| = -(t_1 \cdot t_2) = r^2 - \|Q\|^2$. The dimension-independence is automatic since the proof uses only `InnerProductSpace ℝ E` axioms.
keyInsights: The chord intersection equation in any inner product space reduces to the same monic quadratic $t^2 + 2t\langle Q, \text{dir}\rangle + (\|Q\|^2 - r^2) = 0$, by expanding $\|Q + t \cdot \text{dir}\|^2$ using `inner_add_left`, `inner_smul_right`, and $\|\text{dir}\| = 1$.

Vieta's formula is applied without explicitly computing $t_1$ or $t_2$: subtracting the two quadratic equations gives $(t_1 - t_2)(t_1 + t_2 + 2\langle Q, \text{dir}\rangle) = 0$, and since $t_1 \neq t_2$, we get the sum $t_1 + t_2 = -2\langle Q, \text{dir}\rangle$, which combined with the sum-of-squares from adding the equations gives $t_1 t_2 = \|Q\|^2 - r^2$.

The interior point condition $\|P - O\| < r$ is exactly the condition that $t_1 \cdot t_2 < 0$ (the roots have opposite signs), enabling $|t_1| \cdot |t_2| = -(t_1 t_2) = r^2 - \|P-O\|^2$ via `abs_of_neg`.

The 3D corollary (`sphere3d_chord_products_equal`) converts from geometric distances $\|A_i - P\|$ to absolute parameter values $|s_i|$ using $\|P + s \cdot d - P\| = |s|\|d\| = |s|$ (for unit $d$), then delegates to the general theorem.

The theorem holds in any real inner product space, including infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces — the proof is purely algebraic over the `InnerProductSpace ℝ E` type class with no dimension hypothesis.
prerequisites: NormedAddCommGroup and inner product lemmas (inner_add_left, inner_smul_right, etc.)

sections.title: Research Question and Main Results
sections.summary: Imports and docstring stating the open question (does the intersecting chords theorem extend to 3D spheres?) and answering YES — the proof works in any real inner product space. Lists 4 main theorems: chord quadratic, roots product, sphere power invariant, chord product equality.

sections.title: Part 1: Chord Quadratic Equation
sections.summary: chord_quadratic_sphere: if P + t·dir lies on the sphere of radius r (centered at origin), then t² + 2t⟨P,dir⟩ + (‖P‖² - r²) = 0. Proved by expanding ‖P + t·dir‖² via inner_add_left, inner_smul_right, and ‖dir‖ = 1.

sections.title: Part 2: Vieta's Product Formula and Opposite Signs
sections.summary: chord_roots_product_sphere: two distinct chord parameters t₁ ≠ t₂ satisfy t₁·t₂ = ‖P‖² - r². Derived by subtracting quadratic equations to get t₁+t₂ = -2⟨P,dir⟩, then combining with sum-of-squares. Private chord_roots_opp_signs_sphere: interior point forces t₁·t₂ < 0 (opposite signs).

sections.title: Part 3: Power of a Point in Any Inner Product Space
sections.summary: sphere_power_invariant: the main theorem, |t₁|·|t₂| = r² - ‖P-O‖² for any unit direction. Uses chord_roots_product_sphere + chord_roots_opp_signs_sphere, closed by abs_of_neg and ring. sphere_chord_products_equal: any two chords through P give equal products — immediate from sphere_power_invariant.

sections.title: Part 4: Explicit 3D Corollary
sections.summary: Sphere3D structure (center, radius, radius_pos) and onSphere predicate. sphere3d_chord_products_equal: for chords A₁A₂ and B₁B₂ through interior P of a 3D sphere, ‖A₁-P‖·‖A₂-P‖ = ‖B₁-P‖·‖B₂-P‖. Proof: convert geometric distances to |parameters| via norm_smul + unit direction, then delegates to sphere_chord_products_equal.

sections.title: Conclusion and Summary
sections.summary: Closing docstring summarizing the proof: PA·PB = r² - d² for any secant through interior point P. Dimension-independent via inner product axioms. #check statements for sphere_power_invariant and sphere_chord_products_equal.

conclusion.summary: This file proves 6 theorems (plus 1 private lemma) with 0 sorries and 0 axioms, establishing the power of a point theorem in full generality for any real inner product space, with an explicit 3D corollary.
conclusion.implications: The theorem confirms that the power of a point is a purely inner-product-space phenomenon, valid in any dimension. The proof technique (chord quadratic + Vieta) applies uniformly from $\mathbb{R}^2$ to infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. This is a model example of how type-class polymorphism in Lean 4 enables dimension-free mathematics: the same proof term witnesses the 2D circle case, the 3D sphere case, and the infinite-dimensional Hilbert sphere case simultaneously.
openQuestions: Generalize to complex inner product spaces: does $|t_1| \cdot |t_2| = r^2 - \|P-O\|^2$ hold for complex Hilbert spheres (where inner products are sesquilinear)?
Prove the external case ($P$ outside the sphere): for a secant line, $PA \cdot PB = d^2 - r^2$ where $d = \|P - O\|$ and the product has opposite sign convention.
